title: No Chhath at Rabindra Sarobar without tribunal's nod, minister says; 50 ghats readied
dek: Two days after saying the state would allow Chhath at the protected Kolkata lakes, Agnimitra Paul said she would not go against the environment court. Environmentalists had objected.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Chhath Puja will not be held at Kolkata's Rabindra Sarobar and Subhas Sarobar lakes this year unless the National Green Tribunal permits it, West Bengal's Urban Development and Municipal Affairs Minister Agnimitra Paul has said, stepping back from her announcement two days earlier that the government would allow the festival there.

"If we do not get permission, Chhath Puja will not be held at Rabindra Sarobar," she said, adding that the government could not go against the environment court, according to reports on Friday. At least 50 alternative ghats will be ready in south Kolkata, including at Patuli, Nonadanga, Jodhpur Park and Poddar Nagar, she said. Chhath falls from 13 to 16 November this year.

## How the plan changed

On Wednesday Ms Paul had told reporters: "This year we will allow Chhath Puja at Rabindra Sarobar." She listed conditions, including the immediate removal of all puja materials from the water, paved paths, changing rooms, bio-toilets, lighting and volunteers for crowd control, and said she would discuss the plan with the tribunal. "Where else are the locals supposed to go?" she asked, according to reports. She accused the previous Trinamool Congress government of stopping Hindu festivals for political reasons.

By Wednesday afternoon, after inspecting a water body at Jodhpur Park, she said environmental concerns would be given priority and that 50 water bodies would be used if permission was not granted, reports said. Her department's legal cell is examining the matter. No application to the tribunal or any court has been reported.

Engineers of the Kolkata Metropolitan Development Authority (KMDA), which manages the lakes, urged the state secretariat, Nabanna, not to build ghats there and sent it a copy of the Supreme Court's order, according to reports. One report said Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari did not agree to the proposal, while earlier reports had described it as the chief minister's wish; the government has not issued a written statement.

## Background: a ban upheld in the courts

Rabindra Sarobar, in south Kolkata, is listed as a national lake. The Eastern Zone bench of the National Green Tribunal barred pujas, picnics and other festivities in and around it, including Chhath, in a case brought by environmentalists over damage to the lake. Reports date the ban to 2017 or 2018.

In 2019 about 200 people broke the locks on two gates to perform Chhath at the lake. In September 2020 the tribunal rejected KMDA's request to allow the festival with restrictions. That November the Calcutta High Court ruled, on a petition by environmentalist Subhas Dutta, that both lakes "will be totally out of bounds for Chhath Puja celebrations", and the Supreme Court said it had nothing to add to the High Court's judgment.

## What they are saying

Environmentalists reacted sharply to Wednesday's announcement. "It is a national lake, not a pond," said Somendra Mohan Ghosh of the Save Rabindra Sarobar campaign, according to one report. Naba Dutta, an environmental campaigner, said one cannot do as one pleases just because one has power. Sheikh Soleman of the Paschim Banga Vigyan Mancha, a science forum, said they would take to the streets again if needed. Campaigners have said they will go to court if the government tries to hold the festival at the lakes.

No response from the Trinamool Congress was reported.

## What happens next

The alternative ghats are to be ready before Nahay Khay, the first day of Chhath, on 13 November. Separately, the state's rules for the festival season allow only green firecrackers, between 6 am and 8 am on Chhath.
